reviews.title: 2.0 not intuitive
reviews.text: I struggled my way through adding a couple books and changing the date, having to navigate multiple pages to do so instead of just being able to enter the info as I add the book or simply click on the book I added to edit it. Instead I have to navigate to my profile, find it there and only there can it be edited & they dont show you a calendar as you add dates to make it easier. A hassle that feels unworth the extra effort clearly singularly intended for social media engagement instead of a nice personal log and book suggestions Id hoped for.

reviews.title: Was great until the update
reviews.text:
I loved this app loads when I first found it but since the update it has become complicated. You used to be able to go into a monthly view of your reading sessions and amend previous settings (I often managed to log session under the wrong date) and now you cannot do this

The widgets for iPhone no longer work properly. When logging how much time spent on a reading session amending the time is a nightmare as whenever you try to move the wheel round the whole pop up window tries to move. It feels very much like you took a perfectly functional working app, went backwards, did no testing and made it not functional and called it an “update”

reviews.title: Please change it back!
reviews.text: This was my absolute favorite app before the update. All my reading stats were beautifully laid out in perfect little grids and I could easily compare my reading month to month. I could study it for hours. Now everything is big and clunky and squished and I can’t even see all my books if I’ve read more than 12 in a month. I’m begging you to change it back. And why does every app have to be a social media app? I just want to see my reading stats! I understand it’s still in beta but I’m struggling to even want to open the app now.

reviews.title: Used to be great
reviews.text:
I loved Margins up until their new 2.0 update recently. I had finally found a book tracker that didn’t have major concessions or flaws. 

But this new update basically ruined the app unfortunately. Latency is now horrendous, UI/UX took a nosedive, some features now are unusable due to what seems like any lack of testing.

It was great while it lasted, but in rebuilding the app for android users and to pave the way for more social features, they’ve eliminated all of what made it great.

reviews.title: Super Glitchy
reviews.text: I want to like this app. There are so many features that could be great, but it is just so glitchy. It double records my reads, the descriptions are in French half of the time, and to record past daily reads beyond 5 days you have to have a paid subscription. Too many bugs for me to pay to use this.

reviews.title: Don’t like the updated version
reviews.text: Loved this app until the recent changes. Runs a lot slower, the calendar has moved into a separate section rather than being on the main Home Screen and the dates are wrong (like a previous reviewer said, it’s not including Sundays). Please go back to how it was!

reviews.title: Why update an app without testing it
reviews.text: This is my favourite app for recording what I’m reading, the recent update really makes me want to move to a different app - the main thing I want to see is my calendar of reading, this is now gone from the home page. When you eventually find the calendar the programming of the app has deleted Sunday as a day on the calendar! A very  disappointing update when they don’t let you use the app without updating. Perhaps they should test updates before releasing.

reviews.title: i can't import anything
reviews.text: i want to like this app so bad, god knows goodreads needs better UI upgrades. but i've tried five different times now, and margin only reads my goodreads shelf as empty. i don't know if it's a problem with my location (hong kong) that it's inaccessible or something, but it's so frustrating. i'm deleting this app now.

reviews.title: What the hell is with the profile picture?
reviews.text: I downloaded this app thinking it would help me want to read more, however when logging it and me attempting to put a picture of my cat as my profile picture, it wouldn’t let me. Something about their filter only working on human faces. First of all, that’s idiotic. Second of all, the filter used is very clearly ai, as can be seen when taking a proper look at the details. For an app about reading, I’m extremely disappointed with the ai usage, especially now with the truth about how damaging ai is being common and easily accessible knowledge. Another thing, when I attempted to choose a photo that had only half of my face shown, it somehow found a picture of my full face (which was no where near the original picture i chose, so no chance of me having misclicked and chose that one instead) and used that. That is extremely creepy to me, I do not like how it was able to do that without my consent or input. My point is, the whole filter thing is moronic, to the point it turned me off using the app completely and I deleted it. Please, just let people use what pictures they want to use as their profiles. Better yet, give them the option to choose if they want their face being put through ai or not. Do better.

reviews.title: Too much with too little
reviews.text:
This app has too many shelves and labels, to the point where tracking reading becomes harder instead of easier. The system feels overdesigned and underthought.

I don’t understand why there is a “stopped reading” category in stats, yet no clear “Did Not Finish (DNF)” option. In my opinion, those are not the same thing, and the current wording is vague and confusing for readers who track seriously.

Imported books automatically land on an “unread” shelf, forcing users to manually move them to “want to read.” Why? For most readers, those categories mean the same thing. This extra step adds friction for no reason.

The 2025 Reading Wrapped appeared once and then disappeared entirely. There is no visible way to access it again. Whether this is a bug or a design choice, it’s a major UX failure. If it exists, users should be able to find it easily.

Overall, the app feels like it was designed to label everything instead of serving core reading habits. It prioritizes excessive categorization while missing basic, expected functionality. Sometimes, all a reader needs is Want to Read, Read, and DNF. That’s it.

Margins has real potential, but it currently feels like every idea was added without pruning, while fundamental reading-tracking needs were overlooked. The app is also buggy and slow at times, which only worsens the experience.

This could be a great app, but it urgently needs a UX design team focused on simplicity and clarity.
